title: Need for Speed: Most Wanted (2005)
_about: Most Wanted as the console had it on 2026-10-11: the 1.3 base copy, the DRM-free exe with the
frame-limiter and large-address-aware patches, the ASI loader, XtendedInput, the Widescreen Fix, the
Xbox 360 Stuff Pack 4.2 (no glass shader: it smears interior glass under DXVK), HD Content Support,
HUD Adapter, Front-End Shadows, HD Reflections, Xbox 360 Converted Movies, DSOAL, our two ASIs,
DXVK 3.1.1 lean and native D3DX. Every file is pinned by SHA-256 and taken from
mods-cache/<sha256>[.ext]; the edited files are checked against the console's own (expect).

# NFS Most Wanted — DXVK 3.1.1
# The 360 pack rewrites dynamic buffers the GPU may still be reading; cached
# CPU-side copies keep those locks from waiting on the GPU.
d3d9.cachedDynamicBuffers = True

# prospero-win: the PS5 port takes 48 kHz stereo; a deeper buffer than the default 3 x 1024 for the console's coarser thread wake-ups.
[general]
channels = stereo
frequency = 48000
period_size = 1024
periods = 4
hrtf = false

# 360 Stuff config

[VIDEO]

# Enables custom grass shader. May negatively affect performance
GrassShader = 1

# Enables parallax scrolling on certain surfaces. Some may prefer this to be off.
DoParallax = 1

# Uses car's reflection cubemap for rearview mirror.
# Also enables rendering other cars into cubemap
CubemapRVM = 1

# For performance, Xbox 360 only renders cars into the rear cubemap face
# While slow, this can yield nicer looking results in reflections
# (NOTE: this option is EXPERIMENTAL and may be buggy)
CarsInAllCubemapFaces = 0

# Enables motion blur. Set to 2 to disable depth masking (may slightly improve performance)
MotionBlur = 0

# Enables depth of field in NIS cutscenes and certain game moment cameras
DOF = 1

# Widescreen UI mode
# 0 = Auto-Detect, 1 = Force on, 2 = Force off
WidescreenUIMode = 0

# Disable this if you're using the original PC Movies (16:9 letterboxed to 4:3)
WidescreenMovies = 1

# Changes 3D scaling as it varies between various versions
# (and is almost never mathematically correct leading to varying levels of stretching and squashing)
# 0 = Mathematically correct, 1 = Xbox 360, 2 = PC, 3 = PS3, 4 = Original Xbox,
# 5 = GameCube (NTSC), 6 = GameCube (PAL), 7 = PS2 (NTSC), 8 = PS2 (PAL)
# See "Previews\Scaling" for image comparisons
ScalingMode = 1

# Changes 2D/FE scaling as it varies between various versions
# 0 = Custom/Correct scale, 1 = Xbox 360 scale (in widescreen it is equivalent to 0 with 0.92 scale),
# 2 = PC scale, 3 = PS3 scale, 4 = Original Xbox scale, 5 = GameCube (NTSC) scale,
# 6 = GameCube (PAL) scale,  7 = PS2 (NTSC) scale, 8 = PS2 (PAL) scale
# See "Previews\Scaling" for image comparisons
FEScalingMode = 1

# Sets the scale of the UI when FEScalingMode is 0.
# On Xbox and Xbox 360 in widescreen it is 0.92. On PC and PS2 it is 1.0. On PS3 it is about 0.93 in widescreen.
FEScale = 1.0

# Various parts of the frontend begin to fall apart as the framerate increases above 60fps.
# Enabling this caps the framerate in the frontend to 60 to avoid the issues.
CapFEFramerate = 1

# Makes the sunsets no longer engulf the world in shadow,
# hiding the shortcomings of the LiSPSM shadowmapping technique
# PC hid the issues by fading them out instead.
Xbox360ShadowAngle = 1

# Enables the built-in lite widescreen fix (EXPERIMENTAL)
WidescreenFix = 0

# Sets a custom resolution if widescreen fix isn't present. A value of 0 makes it autodetect the desktop resolution.
XResolution = 0
YResolution = 0

# Enables the game's built-in unused borderless windowed mode
Windowed = 0

[ENHANCEMENTS]

# Xbox 360 doesn't do an actual blur when downscaling for blackbloom, this fixes that
NicerBlackBloom = 1

# Xbox 360 doesn't do an actual blur when downscaling for DOF, this fixes that
NicerDOF = 1

# Xbox 360 uses a depth sorting algorithm for trees, though that doesn't always yield the best results. This forces the use of fixed rendering order values.
FixedTreeRenderOrder = 1

# Xbox 360 uses lowlod shader for traffic and cop cars in the main view. Enable this to use full LOD shader instead.
UseFullLODShaderOnTrafficAndCops = 0

# Xbox 360 sets twkTimeOfDayOvercast in NISes, but rarely ever sets it back properly, causing the weather cycle to freeze until it does
# Enabling this makes the override get reset the next time you return to FE.
# It also nerfs Earl's Earth-rotating powers.
ResetOvercastOverrideAfterNIS = 1

# The Xbox 360 version limits the render distance of cubemaps (except for the rear face as it's used for RVM) to 100m. 
# You can extend it by setting this to a higher value
# 100.0 = Xbox 360, 15000.0 = PC (same as main view, slightly overkill), 300.0 = ProStreet
EnvMapFarPlane = 100.0

# Same as above but for the rear face and RVM. Due to it being used for the mirror it has a bigger distance.
# 400.0 = Xbox 360 (both MW and ProStreet), 15000.0 = PC (same as main view)
MirrorFarPlane = 400.0

# On the 360 version they tried to fix stretching at screen edges during intense motion blur by reversing its direction,
# but they only did it on the Z axis making it appear incorrect diagonally. This fixes that. You can also set it to 2
# to remove the fix altogether and make it more like Carbon where they also did that.
FixDiagonalMotionBlur = 1

[MISC]

# Makes game take screenshots in PNG format instead of TGA
TakePNGScreenshots = 1

# Changes path that screenshots are saved to.
# Example path: %UserProfile%\Documents\NFS Most Wanted
# Defaults to My Pictures folder if path is blank or doesn't exist.
PNGScreenshotPath = %UserProfile%\Documents\NFS Most Wanted

# Sets car lighting (Shaper Light Rig) setup
# 0: Xbox 360
# 1: OPM
# 2: E3-style
# 3: vanilla PC/unmodified (use this if another mod modifies shaper lights)
CarShaperLightType = 0

# Allows cars to self-shadow (NOT how it's intended by devs so don't expect it to look good)
CarSelfShadow = 0

# Enables controller tips screen (VERY broken right now)
EnableLoadingControllerScreen = 0

# Controller tips texture name (_C1 suffix for analog steer, _C2 for dpad steer)
LoadingControllerScreenTextureName = LOADING_CONTROLLER_X360_C1

# Controls the sensitivity of the motion blur to speed
# Default value is 1.0
DirectionalMotionBlurStrength = 1.0

# Xbox 360 has unused angular motion blur, nullified by its strength constant being set to 0
# A recommended value to reenable it would be around 500
# Default value is 0.0
AngularMotionBlurStrength = 0.0

# Allows you to change the minimum shadow projection height
# 0.7 = Xbox 360, 1.0 = nearly straight down, 0.0 = can go down to horizon
# NOTE: this value is approximate as it only changes the Z component of the sun direction vector
# and doesn't change lighting or the sun position itself, only shadowcasting.
# It's not recommended to change this value if you value accuracy.
MinimumShadowAngleHeight = 0.7

# Fixes time of day changes done by NISes on the 360 version.
# Disabling this restores broken PC behavior.
NISTimeOfDayEvent = 1

# Enables the use of the current-gen/PC sun flare instead.
# Only enable this if you like the bigger flare on those versions, or need compatibility with existing sun flare mods.
CurrentGenSunFlare = 0

# The retail Xbox 360 version uses the black bloom curve for both black bloom AND color bloom.
# Enabling this restores what seems to have been early behavior, and what is the retail PC behavior.
# Use this with visual treatment presets tuned for PC visual treatment.
UseColourBloomCurve = 0

# This value affects the brightness of exposure adaptation. It is not recommended to be changed from the Xbox 360 default of 0.14.
# Set this to 0.19 for (roughly) PC-equivalent brightness, which is best paired with the option above.
# NOTE: NISes have the ability to override this value. So far a NIS that does this hasn't been observed, but the capability is there.
MiddleGrayValue = 0.14

# Set this to a value greater than zero to force a constant luminance level. May offer a very slight speedup.
# Setting this to 1.0 and MiddleGrayValue to 0.62 should offer roughly the same constant luminance as PC.
ForcedLuminance = 0.0
